title: Ground truth has wrong values in the Berk-Hath dividend-rate sensitivity table (G11:K14), so a correct answer cannot pass
evidence: The table varies Annual Dividend Rate (C12, 7.0%–9.0% in F10:F14) against Discount Rate (C15, 6.3%–8.3% in G9:K9). Its row-axis cell is F12 '=C12', so the axis points at the table's own input cell. The baked GT values are therefore wrong and not monotonic. GT G10:G14 = 11515.7, 11152.9, 11152.9, 11515.7, 12241.4. Rows 11 and 12 are identical, row 13 equals row 10, and PV falls as the dividend rate rises from 7% to 8%. Recomputing PV(r,10,d*10000,10500) + warrant 736.33 gives the correct column G: 11515.7, 11878.5, 12241.4, 12604.2, 12967.0. GT row 14 (9%) = 12241.4 is really the 8% base case, and GT I12 = 10429.3 against a true 11468.4 (the base case, which should equal the term table's I20 = 11468.4). 20 cells are wrong by up to about 1,700. These are modification cells in the only verifier (weight 1, all-or-nothing: every modification cell must match within 1%). Any agent that computes this table correctly fails the whole task.

In 'Berk-Hath Investment Package', F12 is 8%, I9 is 7.3%, and I12 is hardcoded to 10429.3142071995. Recomputing the package using C19's dividend-PV formula, C20's redemption-PV formula, and C42's warrant value gives 11468.3953341322—the value already shown in I20 for the identical 10-year term and 7.3% discount rate. Rows 11–14 contain additional incorrect values; for example, I11 should be 11122.034958488 rather than 10429.3142071995. These discrepancies exceed the verifier's 1% tolerance. title: Invalid golden values in 'Berk-Hath Investment Package'!G10:K14 and frozen data-table evaluation in verifier
evidence: In `untouched_input_Incorrect SIgn Conventions_input.xlsx`, `'Berk-Hath Investment Package'!G10:K14` is a 2D sensitivity data table (`=TABLE($F$9,$C$12,$F10,$C$15,G$9)`) varying Annual Dividend Rate (`F10:F14`: 7.0%, 7.5%, 8.0%, 8.5%, 9.0%) and Discount Rate (`G9:K9`: 6.3% to 8.3%). In the input file, all 25 cells have a stale cached value of `11432.1670414077`. In `gt_02_golden.xlsx`, these 25 cells are hardcoded floats, making 22 of them required modification cells under `verify_spreadsheetbench2_cells` (weight 1.0). However, the golden values in `gt_02_golden.xlsx` are mathematically wrong: rows 11 and 12 (7.5% and 8.0% dividend rate) both equal the 6.5% dividend rate PV (`G11 = G12 = 11152.88` instead of `11878.54` and `12241.37`), row 13 (8.5%) equals the 7.0% PV (`G13 = G10 = 11515.71` instead of `12604.20`), and row 14 (9.0%) equals the 8.0% PV (`G14 = 12241.37` instead of `12967.03`). Furthermore, `recalculate_xlsx` in `libreoffice.py:553` calls `freeze_datatable_formulas(patched_input)` before running LibreOffice, which strips all `TABLE(...)` formulas and keeps whatever cached `<v>` tags were saved in the file. Thus, leaving the valid `TABLE(...)` formulas intact (as in `DCF!V10:Z14` and `'Berk-Hath Investment Package'!G10:K14`) fails unless the agent manually overwrites the cached values, and computing the true mathematical values for `G10:K14` (as unit 3 did) still fails on 20 of the 25 cells against the buggy golden values.
confirmation: GT Berk-Hath G10:K14 are hardcoded wrong values (G11=G12=11152.88 against true 11878.54/12241.37, G14=12241.37 against 12967.03), and freeze_datatable_formulas keeps only cached values. So neither leaving the TABLE() cells nor computing the true sensitivities matches the 22 modification cells.

title: Correct formula fixes fail the verifier because the data tables are stored as plain TABLE() text that LibreOffice cannot recalculate

The GT replaces them with hardcoded numbers. I applied exactly the GT's formula fixes with openpyxl (the tool the prompt recommends): DCF rows 17/24/26, WACC!C22, Merger Model E29/E57. After the verifier's LibreOffice recalculation every TABLE cell came back empty (None). Score: regression 0.9915 (below the 0.998 threshold, because 50 regression cells in Berk-Hath G18:K30 lost their values) and modification 0.7552, so the result is 0. To pass, an agent must notice this, recompute 50 sensitivity outputs outside the spreadsheet engine and paste them in as hardcodes. That contradicts the prompt's own list of errors, which includes 'hardcoded values that should be formulas'. Nothing tells the agent this is expected.
